2. RepLKNet
What: CNN with very large kernels (up to 31x31!), inspired by the global receptive field of transformers.
Why: Matches or beats ViTs on many vision tasks, still fast and efficient.
Link: RepLKNet Paper
3. HorNet
What: CNN with Horn-shaped convolutional blocks and implicit attention (using gated convolutions).
Why: Outperforms many ViTs and CNNs, especially on segmentation and detection.
Link: HorNet Paper
4. VAN (Visual Attention Network)
What: CNN with large kernel attention (not transformer attention, but similar effect).
Why: Efficient, strong on benchmarks, pure convs.
Link: VAN Paper
5. MetaFormer Family
What: A framework showing that the “transformer” magic is mostly in the architecture, not the attention.
Variants: PoolFormer, ConvFormer, CAFormer, etc.
Why: Some are pure CNNs, some hybrids, all competitive.
Link: MetaFormer Paper
6. ConvMixer
What: Patchify the image, then use depthwise and pointwise convs in a mixer-style architecture.
Why: Stupidly simple, surprisingly strong, pure convs.
Link: ConvMixer Paper
7. SLaK (Sparse Large Kernel Network)
What: Uses sparse large kernels for global context, but keeps computation low.
Why: Efficient, scalable, and SOTA on some tasks.
Link: SLaK Paper
8. FocalNet
What: Combines focal convolutions (focus on both local and global) with a transformer-like block structure.
Why: Hybrid, but with a strong CNN backbone.
Link: FocalNet Paper
